title: Operational Signal Contracts and Lightweight Trace Patterns
content:
Purpose and scope

This is a working note to define a small, pragmatic surface of observability artifacts we will guarantee for token-serving inference paths (hosted + dedicated + private). Goal: provide minimal but actionable signal contracts that SRE, runtime, and product teams can rely on for incident detection, RCA, and capacity planning without exploding cardinality or trace volume.

Why 'lightweight' signals?
- Our tracing budget is finite: avoid full trace capture for every request.
- Many existing dashboards dig into too much dimensionality; we need compact, high-signal metrics and a simple span model for fast debug.
- Focus on SLO-relevant slices and deterministic anchors for session/reconstruction.

High-level design principles
1) One canonical request id per customer request (X-Request-Id) propagated across all layers, attached to metrics and sampled traces.
2) SLI-first metrics: define metrics that map directly to SLOs (latency P95/P99, error-rate, token-throughput per model).
3) Low-cardinality routing tags: tenant_id (coarse bucketed), deployment_tier (hosted/dedicated/private), region, model_family (e.g., llama2-13b), and rollout_tag (canary/stable). Avoid model_version in top-level metrics unless aggregated.
4) Cost-aware sampling: heavier sampling when anomaly detection triggers, otherwise adaptive baseline sampling (0.5% full traces, 5% header-only breadcrumbs).
5) Privacy-aware spans: redact user_prompt when reconstructing traces; capture prompt fingerprints only.

Signal contracts (metric definitions)
- inference.request.count
  * Type: counter
  * Unit: requests
  * Labels: tenant_bucket, model_family, region, route_name
  * Purpose: traffic volume and capacity planning
  * Expected cardinality: low (<= 50 per tenant across all labels)

- inference.tokens.generated
  * Type: counter
  * Unit: tokens
  * Labels: tenant_bucket, model_family, quantization_profile
  * Purpose: cost forecasting and batching efficacy

- inference.request.latency_ms
  * Type: histogram (or summary if necessary)
  * Unit: ms
  * Buckets: [10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000]
  * Labels: tenant_bucket, model_family, route_name, path_phase (router, runtime, kv_cache, gpu_exec)
  * Purpose: SLO monitoring and sliceable drilldowns
  * Cardinality guard: path_phase limited to 5 known values

- inference.errors.count
  * Type: counter
  * Unit: errors
  * Labels: tenant_bucket, model_family, error_class (timeout, oom, mem_error, validation, fallback)
  * Purpose: alerting and incident triage

- kv_cache.hit_fraction
  * Type: gauge (ratio 0..1) aggregated over 5m windows
  * Labels: tenant_bucket, model_family, cache_tier
  * Purpose: measure benefit of prefix caching on latency/cost

- batch.size_distribution
  * Type: histogram
  * Unit: requests-per-batch
  * Labels: model_family, node_pool
  * Purpose: detect batching regressions that increase latency

Tracing: lightweight span model
- Trace fingerprinting: instead of full request capture, attach a short (hex8) fingerprint of the normalized prompt and pipeline config to traces and metrics. The fingerprint is reproducible and reversible only with internal tooling.
- Span naming convention (short):
  * span.root = inference.request
  * span.router = inference.router.route-selection
  * span.cache = inference.kv-cache.lookup
  * span.batch = inference.batch.collect
  * span.exec = inference.gpu.exec
  * span.emit = inference.response.serialize
- Each span should include: start/end timestamps, duration_ms, node_id, model_family, batch_size (if applicable), request_id, tenant_bucket, rollout_tag.
- Breadcrumb header: for unsampled traces, emit a lightweight "breadcrumb" log with request_id, duration_ms, outcome (ok/error), and fingerprint; stored for 7d for cheap drilldowns.

Sampling strategy (practical plan)
- Baseline: 0.5% full traces across all traffic, 5% breadcrumb capture. Configuration is per-deployment_tier.
- Conditional up-sampling: full-trace capture for 100% of requests that hit an error classification > threshold (e.g., error_rate > 0.1% in 1m window) or when anomaly detector flags latency spike for a model_family.
- Canary/rollout: sample 10% of canary traffic to get sufficient signal.

Dashboard wireframes and micro-widgets
- Compact SLO tile: current SLO attainment for inference.p95_latency_ms and error_rate with 7d sparkline and color banding (green/yellow/red).
- Heatmap: model_family vs region latency P95; clickable to open session reconstruction (filtered by tenant_bucket).
- Cost impact widget: tokens.generated * cost_per_token by model_family with trendlines and 30/90d comparisons.
- Breadcrumb table: shows latest 200 breadcrumbs (rotating), columns: ts, request_id, duration_ms, outcome, fingerprint, region, model_family. Click row -> try to retrieve full trace if sampled.
- Batching dashboard: mean batch size, P90 batch wait time, batch size histogram. Alert if mean batch size drops below configured thresholds for model_family.

Alerting and ownership (starter set)
- SRE owns SLO alerts: p95_latency breach for > 3m in a region; page if sustained > 10m and p99 also > threshold.
- Runtime owns infra errors (OOM, mem_error) and high error ratio for specific node_pool.
- Product/PD notified for model_family quality regressions (increase in fallback or hallucination-detection metrics) but not paged initially.

Acceptance criteria for instrumenting a new route (checklist)
- [ ] Add inference.request.count and latency_ms histogram with correct labels
- [ ] Ensure request_id propagation end-to-end and breadcrumb emission
- [ ] Add sampling config to routing layer (default inherit from deployment tier)
- [ ] Dashboard tile added in sandbox org and linked in PR description
- [ ] Add unit tests that assert label cardinality limits and presence of required labels

Open questions and tradeoffs
- Tenant bucketing: how to bucket small tenants vs large customers without losing visibility? Proposal: maintain an explicit top-20 tenant list (by spend) and map all others to "tenant_bucket:small".
- Prompt fingerprint entropy: how to ensure collisions are rare but PII is not reconstructible? Need security review with privacy team.
- Sampling storage cost: breadcrumbs are cheaper but add query complexity. Evaluate estimated storage increase and query latency with current logging backend (Elastic/BigQuery) before rollout.

Next steps and short-term roadmap (90 days)
1) Implement metric stubs for two pilot routes (router and runtime) and add breadcrumb emission (owner: Ethan).
2) Add a dashboard sandbox and iterate with SRE for alert thresholds (owner: Priya).
3) Run a two-week sampling experiment to validate anomaly detection up-sampling (owner: Sofia).
4) Security review for fingerprinting approach and data retention policy (owner: Security Team request).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally prescriptive on label sets and cardinality; the intent is to keep dashboards fast and queries cheap. If you need additional dimensions for a short-term experiment, prefer adding ephemeral logs or a dedicated high-cardinality index rather than bloating the primary metrics stream.
- If you disagree with the 0.5% baseline sampling, bring numbers (cost forecast and query latency) to the next observability sync.

References and related artifacts
- See linked artifacts for PRs and tickets. Also review 'session-reconstruction-patterns' on Confluence for trace join patterns.

Quick glossary
- tenant_bucket: coarse grouping of tenant ids for metric aggregation (top-N + small)
- breadcrumb: minimal event with request_id + small set of fields for cheap reconstruction
- fingerprint: deterministic small hash of normalized prompt/config used to group similar prompts

End of doc.

Revision history:

- 2024-12-12 sampling proposal tweaks (Ethan)
- 2025-02-14 clarified label sets and dashboard widgets (Sofia)
